<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/service-storage`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-storage/src/content-disposition.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/storage-service.mdx`  _(via PresignedDownloadOptions (symbol, a top-level interface), getPresignedDownload (symbol, a method of class S3StorageAdapter))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/storage-service.mdx`  _(via PresignedDownloadOptions (symbol, a top-level interface))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-storage/src/content-disposition.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a3ee8621ede7e60ca49dfe319cb10b86f251480f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `030839e9fa5d73c2478b462ad46bae952a5069ae` — the merge of head `a33cca4e2bf79cde0be6443163a16c82f4b85372` into base `a3ee8621ede7e60ca49dfe319cb10b86f251480f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 030839e9fa5d73c2478b462ad46bae952a5069ae && git checkout 030839e9fa5d73c2478b462ad46bae952a5069ae
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a3ee8621ede7e60ca49dfe319cb10b86f251480f a33cca4e2bf79cde0be6443163a16c82f4b85372 && git checkout -B drift-repro a3ee8621ede7e60ca49dfe319cb10b86f251480f && git merge --no-ff a33cca4e2bf79cde0be6443163a16c82f4b85372

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a3ee8621ede7e60ca49dfe319cb10b86f251480f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a3ee8621ede7e60ca49dfe319cb10b86f251480f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cb1b0d759a37ffdce1c359ecbfaa6ea6e120072d`
Local-runs: probe — one headless Chrome 153 run against a standalone fixture answering this head's exact response header set (no repository code built, run or changed), because whether the allow-listed inline types still render under the answer's CSP can be read from no diff and no check-run
Scope: packages/services/service-storage/src/served-bytes-policy.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/s3-storage-adapter.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/content-disposition.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/served-bytes-policy.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/stored-bytes-served-disposition.dogfood.test.ts + read, not reviewed: service-storage local-storage-adapter.ts, record-file-access.ts, swappable-storage-service.ts, mount-storage-routes.ts, index.ts; packages/spec/src/contracts/storage-service.ts; service-mailbox ingest/mail-ingest-service.ts and parse-message.ts; plugin-email attachment-storage.ts; plugin-hono-server adapter.ts; ui RecordAttachmentsPanel.tsx, ApprovalActionTimeline.tsx, fields file-affordance.tsx and file-value.ts, components containers.tsx

Check-runs on this head (`pr-state.mjs --pr 36518`): 40 success, 15 expected skip, 0 unexpected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes on this head:
- Local raw byte route (`GET /api/v1/storage/_local/raw/:token`): the disposition is a verdict of the allow-list, never of the link's own `d`. The type answered is the recorded type's essence; `charset` survives on `text/plain` only; a missing or non-media-type value answers `application/octet-stream`. `content-disposition` is now always present (bare when the link names no file). `x-content-type-options` and `content-security-policy` ride every 200.
- S3 `getPresignedDownload` / `getSignedUrl`: `ResponseContentType` and `ResponseContentDisposition` are always baked. A call naming no type used to leave the object's own recorded type and no disposition; it now signs `application/octet-stream` as an attachment. A caller's `disposition: 'inline'` no longer overrides the list.
- Unchanged: `IStorageService` signatures, the package exports (the policy module is not re-exported from `index.ts`), every spec schema, the route table, error codes.

Route census, re-derived on the head rather than taken from the PR body:
- storage-routes.ts mounts 12 routes; exactly one writes stored bytes into a response (lines 2161-2198), and it sets all four headers from the rule.
- `GET /files/:fileId` answers a 302 carrying only `Location`; `GET /files/:fileId/url` answers JSON. Both, and the record-file read (record-file-access.ts:925), mint through `mintDownloadUrl`, which reaches only the two adapters' `getPresignedDownload`.
- `storage.download(` has five other callers; none writes to an HTTP response (reference copy, health probe, swappable passthrough, email delivery, and the record-file read handing bytes to the MCP door).
- No thumbnail or preview route exists. `_local/raw` is mounted once.
- HEAD is answered by the same handler (plugin-hono-server adapter.ts:1565-1573), so with the same headers.
- `Range` is not read: whole body, 200, same headers. No validator is sent, so there is no 304 path.
- Error answers are JSON envelopes holding no stored bytes.

Allow-list bypass attempts, none found:
- The answered `content-type` is computed from the same normalised string the verdict is taken on, so no spelling is judged one way and answered another.
- Parameters are dropped before the lookup; case is folded; outer whitespace is trimmed; inner whitespace, a comma-joined pair and control characters fail the media-type grammar and answer `application/octet-stream` as an attachment.
- A non-string type (the token and the request body are JSON) answers `application/octet-stream`.
- The kept `charset` is limited to `[a-z0-9_.:-]`, so it can carry nothing into the header; under `nosniff` a `text/plain` answer stays text.
- The filename and its extension are never consulted for the verdict.
- Lookup is exact-match on an enumerated set; no prefix or suffix rule exists.

`Content-Disposition`: the ASCII form replaces every byte outside 0x20-0x7e, the double quote and the backslash, so no CR, LF or quote reaches the header; the extended form is percent-encoded. An empty name answers the bare disposition. S3 carries the value inside the signed query.

### ② Semver level

- `'@objectstack/service-storage': patch`, the `!` subject, the BREAKING FROM/TO block, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` in both the PR body and the changeset, and the ADR-0087 marker match AGENTS.md Post-Task rule 3: a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` and keeps its banner and disposition.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing a metadata author can write moves.
- `(narrowing)` is the right arm: nothing new is accepted; types formerly rendered in place are now saved.
- One TO sentence is not true as measured: "common audio and video types" are not rendered in place under this head's CSP (M1). The changeset and the docs page must say what the next head does.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. Rule 4 (declared type held to the bytes at upload) — escalated to the maintainer, not ruled here. It is not in this diff and the changeset does not claim it. Options A and B each change a public contract (A adds a storage-contract method and changes the recorded type; B adds a refusal at the upload doors), which is not a reviewer's call. The seat carries the comparison to the maintainer.
2. `nosniff` and the CSP on every answer — keep `nosniff` and the `sandbox` directive on every answer, attachments included. The dev's "no observed cost" does not hold for the `default-src 'none'` half: it has a measured cost on the allow-listed audio and video types (M1).
3. Enumerated allow-list, no prefix match — agreed, keep the enumeration. A prefix would admit types nobody has read. Keeping `charset` on `text/plain` is accepted: the grammar is closed. See N1 for the cost.

Residuals the dev raised:
- A bucket reverse-proxied under the app's own origin: rule 1 travels inside the signed URL and holds; rules 2 and 3 are that proxy's to send. The docs page says the other headers are the bucket's; it does not yet tell an operator who fronts the bucket to send them. Follow-up prose, the seat's to place.
- The spec TSDoc saying inline is the default: S2.

Also read: the dev's full dogfood battery is red in one file (`print-service-render`, 6 tests) on base and head alike, before any storage step; CI skips that file. Not this change.

SQL push-down: the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

M1 (must-fix) — the allow-listed audio and video types do not render in place under the CSP this head sends. Measured in Chrome 153 on a top-level navigation with this head's exact header set: `audio/wav`, `video/mp4` and `video/webm` answer a dead player (`readyState 0`, `networkState 3`), and the console reads "Loading media from … violates the following Content Security Policy directive: default-src 'none'. Note that 'media-src' was not explicitly set". The control, the same answers without the CSP, plays (`readyState 4`, duration 1 s). Consequences: 13 of the 21 list entries do not do what the changeset, the docs page and the module's own doc comment state; the Console's Download on an audio or video attachment now opens a player that never loads, where base played it, and because the answer is `inline` nothing is saved either. No test on the head can see this: both suites pin headers, never a render. Close it one of two ways, measured in a browser: give the policy what a media document needs to load its own URL, or take audio and video off the list so they download. Then pin the behaviour where a browser reads it, and make the changeset, docs and doc comment say what was measured.

S1 (should-fix) — the browser reading covers Chromium alone. In the same probe PNG, `text/plain` and PDF render under the rule, which agrees with the dev's PNG and PDF reading. A PDF under the `sandbox` directive in Firefox and Safari was not measured, and engines differ in how a sandboxed document hosts a built-in PDF viewer. Measure it on the browsers the Console supports, or narrow the changeset's sentence to the engine measured.

S2 (should-fix) — `PresignedDownloadOptions.disposition` in packages/spec/src/contracts/storage-service.ts:225 still reads "`inline` previews in the browser (default)". After this head an adapter answers `attachment` to a caller that asked for `inline` on any type off the list, so the published contract text says more than the runtime does. The dev report lists it with no carrier. Correct the TSDoc on the next head, or file the card before landing and name it in the ACCEPT.

N1 (nit) — common non-registered spellings (`image/jpg`, `image/x-icon`, `audio/mp3`, `audio/x-m4a`) are off the list and download from a tab. That is the safe side and an img element still draws them; a later card if hosts report it.

N2 (nit) — the module comment says a type earns a place "only if no browser executes anything it carries". A PDF can carry script that a viewer runs inside its own sandbox; the sentence wants "nothing that runs with the page's authority".

N3 (nit) — the changeset says parameters do not change the verdict; it does not say the answered type drops them (the PR body does).

First-party surfaces read against the narrowing:
- Console attachments panel and approval timeline open the signed link in a new tab: HTML and SVG now download, as declared; audio and video are M1.
- File, image and avatar fields and the record picture draw through img elements on the stable `/files/:fileId` path. An image element reads neither the disposition nor the document CSP, and SVG keeps its own type, so avatars, logos and SVG images are unaffected.
- No iframe, embed or object element loads a stored file anywhere under `ui/packages` or `ui/apps/console`. The email template preview and the rich-text sanitizer never load stored bytes as a document.
- The print service archives PDF, which is on the list. Email delivery reads bytes server-side. Mailbox ingest records the type the message gives, and the rule judges it at serve time.
- No in-repo caller passes `disposition`, so the override that was removed had no first-party user.
